title: Portuguese reach the Pepper Coast
description: Portuguese sailors open trade on the coast they name the Costa da Pimenta for its malagueta pepper.

title: Freed-slave settlement founded
description: The American Colonization Society lands the first group of freed slaves on Cape Mesurado, bought under duress from the local chiefs.

title: Settlement named Monrovia
description: The main settlement is renamed for the American president James Monroe, a supporter of colonization.

title: Colonies unite in a commonwealth
description: The scattered settler colonies along the coast organise as the Commonwealth of Liberia under a governor.

title: Independence declared
description: Fearing the colonization society cannot protect them from British and French pressure, the settlers declare the free Republic of Liberia, Africa's first republic.

title: Republic of Maryland joins
description: Beleaguered by a Grebo and Kru insurgency, the small settler republic at Cape Palmas joins Liberia as a county.

title: United States recognises Liberia
description: Washington, long loth to recognise the black republic, does so during the Civil War.

title: Firestone rubber concession
description: Firestone gets a ninety-nine-year lease on a million acres for rubber, creating the world's largest plantation and a state within the state.

title: Forced-labour scandal
description: A League of Nations inquiry into the shipment of contract labourers to Fernando Pó forces President King and the vice-president to resign.

title: Tubman inaugurated
description: William Tubman begins twenty-seven years as president, tying Liberia closely to the United States and to foreign investors.

title: Death of Tubman
description: Tubman dies in a London clinic, and Vice-President William Tolbert takes over as discontent simmers under the True Whig state.

title: Rice riots
description: A proposed rise in the price of rice brings crowds into the streets, and troops kill scores of looters and protesters.

title: Doe's coup
description: Master Sergeant Samuel Doe and seventeen enlisted men kill President Tolbert and end 133 years of Americo-Liberian rule.

title: Quiwonkpa's coup fails
description: After a flawed election returns Doe, General Thomas Quiwonkpa's return attempt is crushed and Doe turns on the Gio and Mano.

title: First Civil War
description: Charles Taylor's invasion on 24 December 1989 starts a war that pulverises the country, splits the capital between factions and kills perhaps two hundred thousand people.

title: St Peter's church massacre
description: Government troops massacre some six hundred Gio and Mano refugees sheltering in the St Peter's Lutheran Church.

title: Doe executed
description: Prince Johnson's fighters capture Doe at the ECOMOG headquarters, torture and kill him on camera.

title: Taylor elected president
description: Weary of war, Liberians elect the leading warlord president by a landslide.

title: Second Civil War
description: Rebels of LURD and MODEL, backed from Guinea and Ivory Coast, squeeze Monrovia until the capital falls twice in 2003.

title: Taylor resigns and is exiled
description: Under indictment by the Sierra Leone court and with rebels at the gates, Taylor flies to Nigeria and a transitional government takes over.

title: Sirleaf elected president
description: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf defeats George Weah in the run-off, becoming Africa's first elected female head of state.

title: Taylor convicted of war crimes
description: The Special Court for Sierra Leone convicts the former president of aiding war crimes in Sierra Leone and jails him for fifty years.

title: Ebola epidemic
description: The West African Ebola epidemic kills nearly five thousand in Liberia, shuts down the health system and paralyses the capital.

title: Weah elected president
description: The football star George Weah wins the run-off, and Sirleaf steps down for Liberia's first peaceful transfer between elected presidents in decades.
